reason: Both clear parts bend light, so they look like the starting pieces for the focusing front.
expectation: They will form a front that focuses incoming light.

effect: The cornea and lens now form a focusing front; it still needs a way to control light.
reaction: The rays converging after passing through both parts makes their shared job clear.
reason: The iris has an opening that can narrow, so it should add light control to the focusing front.
expectation: The iris will join the eye front and control how much light enters.

effect: The eye front now focuses light and controls how much enters; the light-sensitive lining remains to be built.
reaction: The picture makes the iris's position and job clear.
reason: The goal calls for a light-sensitive lining with an outgoing nerve, and these cells appear to be its two parts.
expectation: The cells will form a light-sensitive lining connected to outgoing nerve fibres.

effect: The light-sensitive cells and nerve cells form the retina and optic nerve; the two eye parts are ready to join.
reaction: The picture explains how the outgoing fibres gather into a nerve.
reason: The new goal explicitly asks to bring the focusing front and sensing lining together.
expectation: They will form an eye with light focused onto its sensing lining.

effect: The finished eye connects the focusing front to the retina and shows signals traveling toward the brain. All goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the leaf focused on the retina and the parts working together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the eye front and retina was most worthwhile: it brought focusing, sensing and the nerve route together in one picture.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the iris was clear but fairly predictable because its picture already showed the opening narrowing.

surprise.text: I learned that the retina's nerve fibres gather into the optic nerve, rather than just seeing the nerve as a separate cord.

arbitrary.text: None felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals made the pairings understandable.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter: building the eye in two parts and then seeing how they work together was interesting, though the choices were quite straightforward.
